# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the first to observe this round, and I need to establish communication with Blind (who can't see) through Mute. Since Mute speaks first each round, and I go last, whatever I send now will only be seen by nobody this turn (Mute already spoke, Blind already acted before me) — actually let me reconsider: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So I go last. My message now will only be received at the start of next round.

Let me report what I see clearly, since Blind needs this info relayed through Mute (who can hear me) eventually, or I can gesture directly - but Blind cannot see gestures either. So I can only reach Blind through speech, and Blind cannot hear! Wait - check table: Blind cannot see or hear? No, table says Blind cannot see color/gesture/printed things. Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear or touch. Mute cannot speak or touch. Blind cannot see anything visual.

So Blind CAN hear speech. Good - my speech reaches Mute and Blind both. I should describe the bomb clearly in words so Blind can act on it, and Mute can cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 3. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual guidance before any wire is touched.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured "☝" to me — a single raised finger, likely pointing to something specific, perhaps indicating "wire 1" or "step 1" or "one condition matches." Since Mute can't speak to me directly in a way I "hear" — wait, actually Mute cannot speak at all, only gesture. So this gesture is Mute's only way to communicate with me. I can see gestures. This may mean "look at item 1" or "condition one" from the manual.

I don't have enough context to know what "☝" refers to specifically. I should acknowledge and ask for clarification via gesture back, but I can't gesture in a way Mute understands beyond symbols - actually gestures don't carry semantic meaning inherently, we have to build shared meaning. Let me try to establish a simple protocol: I'll gesture back numbers/confirmations using symbols, and describe the bomb state again in speech for Blind's benefit.

Since I can gesture to Mute, let me try acknowledging and asking for more with a numbered gesture system. I'll propose: I gesture "☝" back to confirm receipt, and ask via speech (which Mute can also hear... wait Mute cannot hear either, Mute can only read manual and gesture/receive gestures? Let me check: Mute cannot speak or touch, but can Mute hear? Not stated as cannot, so Mute CAN hear speech.

So Mute hears my speech. Good - I can talk to Mute via speech, and receive from Mute via gesture only.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 3, light green, wires red green blue in order 1 2 3. Gesture which wire number is safe using pointing symbols, one at a time.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute repeated "☝" again — same single gesture. This could mean "wire 1" as an answer to my question, or it could mean Mute is stuck repeating because they haven't received my speech yet (turn timing: my speech this round only lands next round). Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute speaks/acts first, then Blind, then me. So in Turn 2, Mute's gesture was sent before my speech in Turn 2 was processed - meaning Mute hasn't seen my request yet. This "☝" in Turn 3 is likely still Mute's independent action, possibly repeated because Mute is also trying to establish contact, or it's the same message persisting.

Actually my speak(to="mute") from Turn 2 should reach Mute at the start of Turn 3 (next round). So Mute's gesture in Turn 3 was made using info from Turn 2's board only, before receiving my Turn 2 speech (since Mute goes first in the round, before my message arrives). So this ☝ is likely Mute's initial independent attempt again, or a continued signal meaning "wire 1" consistently from the manual matching display=3, light=green.

I'll treat ☝ as "wire 1" candidate answer. Let me confirm by asking Mute directly and also inform Blind in speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received your one-finger sign twice, I think you mean wire number 1. If wire 1 is correct reply again with one finger. If wire 2, use two fingers. If wire 3, three fingers.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute has now sent "☝" three times in a row, consistently. This strongly suggests it's a stable answer: wire 1. Since Mute hasn't varied the gesture despite my request for confirmation (which they may not have received yet due to timing), the consistency itself is meaningful — it's likely the manual's answer for this exact bomb state (display 3, light green) and Mute is just repeating it each turn since the board hasn't changed.

I should now relay this to Blind clearly via speech, since Blind can hear me and needs to know which wire to cut/act on.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has consistently signaled wire number one. Bomb state: display shows 3, light is green, wires are red, green, blue in positions 1, 2, 3. I believe wire 1, the red wire, is the one to act on. Wait for Mute's confirmation before cutting if possible, but this signal has been repeated three times unchanged.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","👍"])
```
